name: Active inflammation and worsening cardiovascular symptoms survive routine steroid plan
rationale: Current worsening symptoms require assessment/delay and cannot be replaced by routine steroids that could oppose immune activation; retain the pre-existing monitoring risks.

name: Current severe respiratory reaction with asthma and resolved-restart tick
rationale: The current severe respiratory event requires discontinuation of administration; a general restart confirmation cannot erase it or the prior-event review.

name: Restart prescription above reference with conflicting renal band and Child-Pugh B
rationale: Severe renal data absence and limited hepatic safety data require review; neither a reassuring categorical band nor a completed restart checkbox supplies a dose.

name: Weekly phase short interval with simultaneous lipophilic drug and high-dose NSAID
rationale: Later weekly timing, administration separation and high-dose NSAID contraindication are separate constraints; one overall outcome must not hide their rationale.

name: Missed-dose extension after chemotherapy with neutropenia and monitoring absent
rationale: Incomplete infusion count does not authorise extension beyond the reference calendar; continue renal/liver monitoring and do not import a cytotoxic ANC hold for isolated neutropenia.

name: Forty-eight infusions with severe hepatic category and contradictory low renal band
rationale: Reference infusion total is reached even before week36; conflicting renal entries and severe hepatic data absence must remain explicit, with no calculated extra dose.

name: Correct preparation filter does not validate IV bolus or in-line administration filter
rationale: The supplied filter belongs to preparation; the liposomal medicine is infused over60 minutes and in-line administration filtration is not recommended.

name: Prolonged post-infusion fever despite non-acute flag and no severe reaction grade
rationale: Fever lasting over8hours requires sepsis evaluation independently of the acute-illness flag and infusion-reaction grade.

name: Ewing baseline with all supportive prerequisites and retained reduced daily prescription
rationale: The source 3000mg/m² daily reference is distinct from a recorded lower2400mg/m² prescription. Correct indication/support/product information must not cause an automatic re-escalation.

name: Relapsed osteosarcoma listed but specialist eligibility plan not confirmed
rationale: Osteosarcoma is an explicit indication but detailed source eligibility prose is Ewing-specific. Require review without importing Ewing timing into osteosarcoma.

name: Relapsed osteosarcoma documented plan with first-cycle source schedule
rationale: A documented osteosarcoma-specific plan removes the encoding gap. The same5-day ifosfamide schedule and distinct day6 mesna remain visible.

name: Current low ANC with prior febrile nadir and severe mucositis history
rationale: Current ANC delay dominates future80% discussions. Two prior-toxicity considerations must not compound to64% or rebase the known2400mg/m² dose.

name: Current thrombocytopenia and active severe mucositis during fluid accumulation
rationale: Active toxicity/count delay and fluid review coexist. No future reduction substitutes for assessment during active severe mucositis.

name: Recovered counts at restart retain both FN and severe mucositis dose history
rationale: Recovery changes current hold status but preserves prior80% considerations and actual reduced dose; do not multiply or automatically re-escalate.

name: Intermediate counts plus prior mucositis and low CrCl with verified normal product labs
rationale: Separate NCCP intermediate count80%, mucositis80% and renal clinical-decision pathways require one reconciled prescription; normal product labs do not erase the CrCl decision.

name: Ongoing hydration with low urine output and increasing weight despite plan tick
rationale: A confirmed hydration prescription does not establish adequate urine output or safe fluid balance. Source hydration/diuresis is clinical assessment rather than automatic furosemide.

name: Haematuria and urinary obstruction despite completed urine assessment and mesna
rationale: The completed check records an abnormal result. Mesna prophylaxis does not permit bypassing new urothelial toxicity or obstruction assessment.

name: Aprepitant and nephrotoxic interaction with dialysis despite reassuring CrCl
rationale: Dialysis is categorical context and cannot be cancelled by a numeric CrCl. Concurrent medicines need individual review without an invented dose.

name: Completed maximum course with prior FN and reduced current prescription
rationale: Four completed cycles is the maximum reference course; history and dose reduction do not authorise an extra cycle.

name: Current infection during recovery despite counts and prior event now resolved
rationale: Recovered counts do not rule out current infection; historical FN reduction does not treat the acute event.

name: Legacy febrile-neutropenia label with missing nadir at non-acute restart
rationale: A generic FN label with current acute event excluded still lacks the combined prior ANC/fever source criterion; do not infer80%.

name: Oral final mesna independently verified while new low urine output persists
rationale: A verified oral final prescription resolves only route reconciliation; it cannot clear current hydration/renal problems.

name: Current severe mucositis with explicit other nonhaematological grade and normal counts
rationale: Named active severe mucositis supplies a source-specific toxicity pathway; no numeric80% dose is generated during unresolved toxicity.

name: Isolated other grade3 ongoing toxicity with full treatment safeguards
rationale: The supplied current significant other-toxicity grade is accepted input but not a named-event definition. Require explicit clinical clarification/review under unacceptable-toxicity continuation language; this expectation does not invent a universal grade3 hold or percentage.

name: Explicit false indication criteria during ongoing treatment
rationale: Known negative source eligibility confirmation during treatment should require clarification even when prior course has started; missing historical context is not being tested.

name: Recovery-stage indication unresolved with an explicit requested restart
rationale: A restart request cannot silently turn explicit false source eligibility into a normal entered value; no new indication or dose is inferred.

name: Severe hepatic category plus absent G-CSF despite otherwise verified product and labs
rationale: A lower entered dose does not make severe hepatic impairment recommended or replace mandatory cycle G-CSF. Keep reasons distinct without resolving product/source authority.

name: Cycle4 planning with prior mucositis, new haematuria and no numerical re-escalation
rationale: The fourth planned cycle is within the course count but current haematuria still withholds; prior toxicity and interaction risk do not create an extra multiplication or re-escalation.
